name: buddhism
followers: about 500 million, mostly in east and southeast asia
founder: siddhartha gautama, the buddha, "the awakened one"
scriptures: the pali canon (tipitaka); many mahayana sutras; the tibetan canon
places: lumbini, bodh gaya, sarnath, and kushinagar, the places of the buddha's life
summary: the path taught by the buddha to end suffering, through understanding its causes, living ethically, and training the mind. it does not depend on a creator god.
creation: the buddha set aside the question of how the world began as not helpful for ending suffering. buddhist texts describe countless world systems that form, last, decay, and form again.
age: time has no known beginning. it is measured in kalpas, eons so long that a mountain wiped with a silk cloth once a century would wear away first. many buddhas have come in past eons, and one, maitreya, is still to come.

events.text: the buddha teaches that no first beginning of the round of rebirth can be found. world systems without number arise, last, decline, and pass away
each world passes through four long stages: forming, lasting, falling apart, and emptiness, and then forms again
the ascetic sumedha meets the buddha dipankara and vows to become a buddha himself. over countless lives he perfects generosity, patience, and wisdom, as told in the jataka tales
the future buddha waits in heaven for the right time, then chooses to be born as prince siddhartha
queen maya gives birth to siddhartha in the lumbini garden. the baby takes seven steps, and a sage foretells he will be either a great king or a buddha
most historians place the buddha's birth around 480 bce at lumbini, in modern nepal; the theravada tradition dates it to 623 bce
outside the palace, siddhartha sees an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering holy man. he leaves his family and his wealth to seek the end of suffering
sitting under the bodhi tree at bodh gaya, he overcomes the tempter mara and wakes up to the truth: he is now the buddha
in the deer park at sarnath, the buddha teaches the four noble truths to five companions, who become the first monks
after 45 years of teaching, the buddha passes into final nirvana at kushinagar
according to tradition, 500 monks meet to recite the teachings together; they are passed down by memory for centuries
the emperor ashoka turns to buddhism after the slaughter at kalinga and sends teachers across and beyond india, including his son mahinda to sri lanka
monks in sri lanka write down the teachings in the pali language, the pali canon of theravada buddhism
buddhism reaches china along the silk roads; by tradition the white horse temple is founded at luoyang
mahayana sutras, such as the lotus sutra and the perfection of wisdom, appear, teaching the path of the bodhisattva
nagarjuna teaches that all things are empty of fixed, separate existence
buddhism reaches korea
the monastery university of nalanda is founded in india; it will draw students from all over asia
a korean king sends an image of the buddha and sutras to japan
the chinese monk xuanzang walks to india to collect scriptures and brings back hundreds of texts
samye, the first buddhist monastery in tibet, is completed
the great stupa of borobudur is built on java
the diamond sutra is printed in china, the oldest dated printed book
invaders destroy nalanda; buddhism fades away in most of india
dogen returns from china and brings soto zen to japan
the fifth dalai lama becomes the ruler of tibet
b. r. ambedkar and about half a million dalits become buddhists at nagpur, rejecting caste
the fourteenth dalai lama flees chinese rule in tibet and settles in india
about 500 million buddhists live mostly in east and southeast asia; buddhist meditation has spread worldwide
when the teaching has been forgotten, maitreya, the next buddha, will be born and teach the path again

people.name: dipankara
people.role: a buddha of the distant past
people.about: the buddha before whom sumedha vowed to become a buddha

people.name: maya
people.about: dreamed of a white elephant before the buddha's birth and died seven days after it

people.name: siddhartha gautama
people.about: a prince who gave up everything to find the end of suffering, and taught the middle way for 45 years

people.name: yasodhara
people.about: raised their son rahula after siddhartha left, and later joined the order of nuns

people.name: mahapajapati
people.dates: aunt and foster mother of the buddha
people.about: persuaded the buddha to let women join the order

people.name: ananda
people.about: remembered all the buddha's sermons; many sutras begin "thus have i heard" in his words

people.name: ashoka
people.about: carved edicts on rocks and pillars urging kindness and tolerance, and helped spread buddhism across asia

people.name: nagarjuna
people.about: founder of the middle way school of mahayana philosophy

people.name: buddhaghosa
people.role: monk and scholar in sri lanka
people.about: wrote the path of purification, the great guide of theravada buddhism

people.name: bodhidharma
people.about: by tradition brought chan (zen) meditation to china and sat facing a wall for nine years

people.name: xuanzang
people.about: walked to india and back, and spent the rest of his life translating the texts he brought home

people.name: padmasambhava
people.about: remembered in tibet as guru rinpoche, who helped found samye and tamed the local spirits

people.name: milarepa
people.about: turned from black magic and murder to become tibet's most beloved saint

people.name: dogen
people.about: taught that "just sitting" in meditation is itself awakening

people.name: nichiren
people.about: taught that chanting the name of the lotus sutra is the way to buddhahood

people.name: b. r. ambedkar
people.about: born into an "untouchable" family, he wrote india's constitution and led a mass conversion to buddhism

people.name: thich nhat hanh
people.about: worked for peace during the vietnam war and taught mindfulness around the world

people.name: tenzin gyatso
people.about: spiritual leader of tibetan buddhism, living in exile in india since 1959; nobel peace prize 1989

people.name: maitreya
people.about: now waiting in the tushita heaven, he will come when the present teaching has been forgotten

glossary.definition: "not-self": the teaching that there is no fixed, unchanging self inside a person.
a being on the way to buddhahood; in mahayana, one who puts off final nirvana to help all beings.
"awakened one": someone who has fully understood the truth. the buddha of our age is siddhartha gautama.
the leading teacher of the gelug school of tibetan buddhism, believed to be reborn in each generation.
in buddhism, the teaching of the buddha and the truth it points to.
suffering, or the unsatisfactory nature of life, the first of the four noble truths.
the way to end suffering: right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, and concentration.
life involves suffering; suffering comes from craving; it can end; and the eightfold path is the way.
an eon, a span of time so long it can only be described by comparisons.
intentional action, which shapes a person's future in this life and in rebirth.
"the great vehicle": the branch of buddhism of china, korea, japan, and vietnam, centered on the bodhisattva.
training the mind in calm and insight, at the heart of buddhist practice.
"blowing out": the end of craving and suffering, and freedom from rebirth.
the community of monks and nuns, and in a wider sense all buddhists.
a domed monument holding relics of the buddha or a saint.
a discourse of the buddha, or a text believed to record his teaching.
"the way of the elders": the branch of buddhism of sri lanka, myanmar, thailand, laos, and cambodia.
"the diamond vehicle": the buddhism of tibet, mongolia, and bhutan, with special rituals and teachers.
a school of mahayana buddhism, chan in chinese, that stresses meditation and sudden insight.
